answer: An enrollment service verifies a fresh SGX/SEV attestation and binds an enclave-held key to the reported MRENCLAVE, using a registry to reject duplicate keys. This makes copying an identity by spinning up virtual machines insufficient: an attacker must obtain valid hardware-backed attestations and keys, raising the cost toward acquiring physical silicon. MRENCLAVE is a code measurement, not a unique device ID, so this anchor deters cheap Sybil creation but does not stop multiple enclaves on one host from wandering through the canyon of identities.
